status: Analyst hypotheses for screening; not observed adoption, WTP or industry-specific efficacy. Root owns final interpretation.
ranking_basis: Relevant recurring workflow cost, ability to amortize integration, reachable budget owner and procurement friction. Margins provide context, not ranking weights or purchasing evidence.

ranked_beachheads.segment: Vertical B2B SaaS and operational software vendors
ranked_beachheads.buyer: Engineering or product leader owning several interactive customer workflows
ranked_beachheads.fit: Repeated client-state coordination and investigation work can be reused across customers. One vendor purchase may serve many downstream firms.
ranked_beachheads.integration_friction: Low for a new module; medium to high for an established platform
ranked_beachheads.paid_budget_hypothesis: mid or enterprise account tier only when attributable labor benefits exceed integration and subscription cost
ranked_beachheads.v15_role: State and entity coordination where existing contracts are sufficient
ranked_beachheads.v16_incremental_role: Long-lived proposals and coordinated publication when useful work overlaps asynchronous approval or delivery
ranked_beachheads.private_tooling_role: Correlating owner, entity lifetime and command evidence with existing logs
ranked_beachheads.first_falsifier: Measure actual state-related maintenance and investigation hours on one production workflow; reject savings that existing tracing already provides.
ranked_beachheads.bad_fit: A simple form or a vendor whose debugging costs concern only remote model quality or database behavior.

ranked_beachheads.segment: Fintech and insurance operations software teams
ranked_beachheads.buyer: Platform or application engineering owner, with operational control owner
ranked_beachheads.fit: Conflicting edits, uncertain completion and command attribution have a plausible operational role; service-side authorization and durable effects remain necessary.
ranked_beachheads.profit_context_sector: Insurance (General); Bank (Money Center) are broad context only
ranked_beachheads.integration_friction: Medium for a new internal workbench; high for regulated legacy platforms
ranked_beachheads.paid_budget_hypothesis: mid or enterprise, contingent on a reviewable deployment and existing vendor requirements
ranked_beachheads.v16_incremental_role: Coordinated pending state and publication while authoritative services settle approved commands
ranked_beachheads.private_tooling_role: Investigation evidence, subject to privacy and retention requirements
ranked_beachheads.first_falsifier: Time recent state-correlation investigations and the extra review/retention burden; price only the portion local context can change.
ranked_beachheads.bad_fit: Claims that SignalTree itself prevents fraud, satisfies financial regulation or makes payments transactional.

ranked_beachheads.segment: Logistics, field-service and industrial operations software vendors or larger internal teams
ranked_beachheads.buyer: TMS/ERP product engineering owner or internal digital operations team
ranked_beachheads.fit: Concurrent edits and delayed acknowledgements resemble the tested dispatch application, but that resemblance is not a customer outcome study. Selling through software vendors may amortize engineering across fleets.
ranked_beachheads.profit_context_sector: Trucking; Machinery are separate broad contexts
ranked_beachheads.integration_friction: Medium for a new console; high for legacy ERP/TMS integration
ranked_beachheads.paid_budget_hypothesis: mid for a focused team; enterprise only for multiple evidenced workflows
ranked_beachheads.v16_incremental_role: Pending coordinated changes where several actors or services operate on the same entities
ranked_beachheads.private_tooling_role: Investigate stale/replayed/uncertain commands across UI and backend
ranked_beachheads.first_falsifier: Measure dispatch exception volume and hours attributable to application-state ambiguity, excluding driver delay or freight losses without a demonstrated causal path.
ranked_beachheads.bad_fit: Small carriers without engineering teams, tiny state surfaces or thin margins paired with expensive migration.

ranked_beachheads.segment: Enterprise manufacturing, wholesale and commerce back-office application teams
ranked_beachheads.buyer: Internal platform owner funding one bounded operational console
ranked_beachheads.fit: Repeated transactional user interactions can create value, but existing ERP, workflow and state investments raise replacement costs.
ranked_beachheads.profit_context_sector: Machinery is illustrative, not a proxy for all manufacturers or merchants
ranked_beachheads.integration_friction: High unless introduced at a planned module boundary
ranked_beachheads.paid_budget_hypothesis: mid or enterprise after measured marginal benefit against incumbent tooling
ranked_beachheads.v16_incremental_role: Only workflows needing the additional coordinated pending contract
ranked_beachheads.first_falsifier: Compare an incremental adapter/new module against whole-store migration, including parallel support and regression qualification.
ranked_beachheads.bad_fit: Replacing stable ERP state wholesale to obtain a small debugging convenience.

ranked_beachheads.segment: Healthcare IT vendors building administrative workflows
ranked_beachheads.fit: Operational state ambiguity may matter, but privacy, data minimization and deployment review can dominate integration cost. Direct clinical use is outside this evidence.
ranked_beachheads.profit_context_sector: Heathcare Information and Technology; Healthcare Support Services are distinct
ranked_beachheads.paid_budget_hypothesis: enterprise only if the deployment requirements are actually supported; otherwise no sale assumed
ranked_beachheads.v15_role: Ordinary state/entity coordination in bounded administrative modules
ranked_beachheads.v16_incremental_role: Coordinated pending state where the application requires it
ranked_beachheads.private_tooling_role: Minimized, scoped evidence with a separately validated retention policy
ranked_beachheads.first_falsifier: Establish a lawful, acceptable data flow and measure operational labor; do not monetize clinical errors or regulatory penalties.
ranked_beachheads.bad_fit: Clinical decision correctness, a substitute for health-data controls, or a low-budget provider without its own software team.

comparators.category: Other public state libraries and native framework state
comparators.relationship: Direct alternatives for some client-state work; full contracts differ
comparators.cost_treatment: Assume zero displaced runtime license fee; compare engineering, measured performance and migration.
comparators.limit: Do not infer equivalent guarantees or universal uniqueness from feature names.

comparators.relationship: Primarily complementary; private investigation tooling partly overlaps
comparators.cost_treatment: Keep existing subscription and usage costs unless a specific tested removal is justified. Count only additional labor benefit.
comparators.limit: Runtime-owner evidence does not evaluate model reasoning or output correctness.

comparators.relationship: Complementary instrumentation and troubleshooting context with partial tooling overlap
comparators.cost_treatment: No full monitoring bill is credited as saved. Include incremental capture, storage and review cost.
comparators.limit: OpenTelemetry is instrumentation/transport, not hosted storage; interoperability is a candidate integration, not a claimed present feature.

comparators.relationship: Backend complement; may compete with custom application orchestration code, not be replaced by local state
comparators.cost_treatment: No assumed savings in workflow-engine subscriptions, durable effects or authentication.
comparators.limit: Browser-owned coordination is not durable external authority.

pricing_and_readiness: Public runtime remains free under its existing license. No paid runtime toll, retroactive license change or paid-user conversion is assumed.
Private Studio, hosted retention, support or integration are separate potential offers. A modeled price is not an offer, commitment or proof of capability.
An enterprise price requires enterprise delivery capacity. No present SLA, certification, SSO, hosting region or procurement readiness is inferred.
Buyer WTP remains unobserved; a calculated maximum affordable price is a conditional value ceiling, not demonstrated demand.
Current private Studio evidence is broader for v16. v15 only has narrow transaction-delegation checks; full Studio-v15 qualification is unestablished.
Hosted multi-tenant delivery, production identity integration and commercial SLAs are not established. Enterprise amounts are future-package hypotheses requiring additional build and support cost.
Widespread free-runtime adoption incurs maintenance/community-support costs. It produces no license revenue in this model.

eligibility.reason: No source connects firm/developer counts to supported interactive applications, relevant recurring pain, integration feasibility and a paid tooling budget. Public counts cannot complete that chain.
eligibility.unit: one paying organization/account; downstream users and deployments are separate denominators
necessary_conditions: Supported application architecture and an owner able to integrate it
A recurring coordination or investigation problem within the demonstrated local/application boundary
A measurable incremental advantage over existing state, tracing and workflow tools
Acceptable performance, privacy, retention and support requirements
Sufficient recoverable labor or separately validated nonlabor risk benefit to cover total cost
eligibility.conditional_counts_mean: Sensitivity assumptions for eligible paying accounts, not a forecast or measured addressable population.
eligibility.aggregation_limit: Do not count the same engineering benefit at both the software vendor and all downstream customers. Deduct customer integration and operations plus supplier real resource costs; subscription payments are transfers in a joint-system calculation.

negative_fit_cases: Simple CRUD, static websites, read-only dashboards and low-incident projects
Backend-only agents needing durable workflow orchestration without interactive state
Model-quality or prompt-injection problems without an attributable state-coordination mechanism
Stable legacy stores whose migration and training cost exceed incremental benefit
High-volume short-lived stores when measured startup cost violates the application budget
Sensitive-data deployments whose retention/control requirements are not yet supported
Tiny teams satisfied by free runtime and free existing observability
Buyers seeking certification, autonomous error prevention or guaranteed business correctness

local_evidence.meaning: Supports tested application boundaries and limits, not human comprehension, production incident reduction or savings.
